consensus_summary: Consensus identifies milk primarily as elementary spiritual teaching or pure nourishment for immature believers (contrasted with solid food/meat for the mature), with OT abundance ('milk and honey') as a distinct secondary sense.
book_summary: Book identifies milk as the word received before interpretation, proper food for babes but meant to be worked/tested/outgrown; churned milk becomes butter, which counts as meat.
consensus_core_identification: Elementary doctrine/pure spiritual nourishment for spiritual infants
book_core_identification: Uninterpreted word as babes' food, destined to be processed into butter/meat
boundary_disagreement: Book keeps milk-as-babes'-food but requires it be churned into butter (reclassified as meat), so the milk/meat contrast becomes a transformative process rather than a static maturity binary; cases of permanent or unprocessed milk-as-nourishment are excluded.
rationale: Both share the same central NT referent (milk = basic word/teaching for babes, per 1 Cor 3, Heb 5, 1 Pet 2). Book preserves that category while materially tightening conditions (must be worked/outgrown) and reclassifying the product (butter = meat via Prov 30:33/Isa 7:15), producing a refined boundary without replacing the core.
strongest_objection: The butter-as-meat step could be viewed as introducing a distinct alchemical referent not entailed by the consensus milk/meat contrast, risking over-reading of Prov/Isa.
